top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson; B038) is a specific, well-identified discovery: import competition and technological change produced large, concentrated and persistent local labour-market adjustment costs, which changed research and policy debate. The design is transparent, and more than a decade of replication and critique lets durability be judged. Attribution is defensible once the citation is limited to exposure and local adjustment and Dorn is the third name, with the task-framework lineage left unclaimed. The shift-share and magnitude debates are a real discount on point estimates, but they have refined practice without overturning the qualitative finding. P004 (Grossman-Helpman) has the cleanest credit and is mature, but the empirical record of Protection for Sale is mixed. P003 (Chetty, Hendren, Friedman) has exceptional measurement and design, but it is younger and relies on restricted data. P002 has clean attribution but only indirect empirical content. P005 has the loosest credit, given the uncredited parallel contributors and Helpman's overlap with P004. No award ranks last because several candidates meet the common criteria.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. My listed co-authors (Holmlund, Edin, Åslund, Öckert, Johansson, Nybom, Oosterbeek, van Ours) are not credited on any proposal. My 2013 class-size paper is cited in the 2021 Scientific Background, which places me in the same research tradition as P001 and P003 but is not a tie to any 2026 candidate. I have a methodological affinity with natural-experiment and register-based work, which I have discounted. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
